metadata.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbor: Towards Removing the Curse of Dimensionality
metadata.authors: Sariel Har-Peled, Piotr Indyk, Rajeev Motwani
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: Registry expected 'Similarity estimation techniques from rounding algorithms' (Charikar, SimHash, 2002); actual PDF is 'Approximate Nearest Neighbor: Towards Removing the Curse of Dimensionality' by Har-Peled, Indyk, Motwani 2012. Extraction performed on the actual paper present.

nodes.name: $c$-approximate nearest neighbor problem ($c$-NN)
nodes.statement: Construct a data structure over points $P$ in metric space $(X,D)$ that, for any query $q \in X$, reports a $c$-approximate nearest neighbor of $q$ in $P$ with probability $1-f$.
nodes.statement_clean: Definition of the c-approximate nearest neighbor problem with allowable failure probability f.

nodes.name: $(c,r)$-approximate near neighbor problem ($(c,r)$-NN)
nodes.statement: Construct a data structure over $P$ in $(X,D)$ such that, given query $q$, if $D_P(q) \le r$ then it reports some $p' \in P \cap B(q,cr)$ with probability $1-f$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the radius-restricted decision-version of approximate nearest neighbor.

nodes.name: Oblivious randomized $(r,c)$-NN data structure
nodes.statement: A randomized fully dynamic $(r,c)$-NN data structure $Z$ with failure probability $f$ is oblivious if for any well-formed sequence $S$, $\Pr[\text{the last operation in } S \text{ is executed correctly}] \ge 1-f$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines oblivious correctness model: each individual operation is correct with high probability.

nodes.name: Adaptive randomized $(c,r)$-NN data structure
nodes.statement: $Z$ is adaptive with respect to $P,Q$ if $\Pr[Z \text{ is correct for any well-formed sequence } S \text{ wrt } P,Q] \ge 1-f$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines adaptive model: with high probability, the data structure is correct on every operation in every adversarial sequence.

nodes.name: Locality-sensitive family of hash functions
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{H} = \{h : X \to U\}$ is $(r_1, r_2, p_1, p_2)$-sensitive for $(X,D)$ if for any $p,q \in X$: $D(p,q) \le r_1 \Rightarrow \Pr_\mathcal{H}[h(p)=h(q)] \ge p_1$, and $D(p,q) > r_2 \Rightarrow \Pr_\mathcal{H}[h(p)=h(q)] \le p_2$.
nodes.statement_clean: LSH definition: hash family that distinguishes near from far points by collision probability.

nodes.name: Geometric Minimum Spanning Tree (MST)
nodes.statement: Given $n$ points in $\ell_s^d$, compute (an approximation of) the minimum spanning tree of the complete weighted graph whose edge weights are pairwise distances.
nodes.statement_clean: Compute the minimum spanning tree of n points under an l_s norm.

nodes.name: Approximation of $r_{\mathrm{med}}$
nodes.statement: There exists a randomized algorithm that, given $n$ points and distance $D$, returns $r^*_{\mathrm{med}}$ with $r_{\mathrm{med}} \le r^*_{\mathrm{med}} \le (n-1)\,r_{\mathrm{med}}$ with probability $\ge 1/2$, in time $O(n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: An O(n)-time randomized algorithm yields a factor-(n-1) approximation of r_med with probability 1/2.

nodes.name: Bounds on connected components when $r^*_{\mathrm{med}}$ is correct
nodes.statement: If $r_{\mathrm{med}} \le r^*_{\mathrm{med}} \le (n-1)\,r_{\mathrm{med}}$, then each connected component of $UB_P(r^*_{\mathrm{bot}} c)$ has $\le n/2$ points, and $CC_P(r^*_{\mathrm{med}})$ contains a component of size $\ge n/2+1$.
nodes.statement_clean: When the median-radius estimate is correct, the connected-component partitioning has the size properties needed for the divide-and-conquer reduction.
conclusions: Each connected component of $UB_P(r^*_{\mathrm{bot}} c)$ has at most $n/2$ points
There is a component in $CC_P(r^*_{\mathrm{med}})$ of size $\ge n/2+1$

nodes.name: Correctness of A PPROXIMATE CC
nodes.statement: Algorithm A PPROXIMATE CC computes a partition $\mathcal{P}$ with $CC_P(r) \sqsubseteq \mathcal{P} \sqsubseteq CC_P(cr)$, runs in time $O(T(n,c,f) + nD(n,c,f) + nQ(n,c,f))$, and fails with probability $\le f$.
nodes.statement_clean: The connected-components subroutine produces a partition between the exact and approximate CC, with the stated time and failure bounds.

nodes.name: Interval near neighbor (INearNbr)
nodes.statement: For $1/2 > \gamma > 0$, $c \ge 1$, range $[a,b]$, one can build $M = O((\log(b/a))/\gamma)$ NearNbr data structures (each with failure $f = 1/(3 \log M)$) so that for any query $q$ one decides one of: $D_P(q) \le a$, $D_P(q) \ge b$, or returns $p'$ with $D(q,p') \le c(1+\gamma) D_P(q)$, correctly with probability $\ge 2/3$.
nodes.statement_clean: INearNbr: a binary-searchable bank of near-neighbor structures resolving the query into one of three outcomes.

nodes.name: Total points stored in INearNbr structures
nodes.statement: The number of points stored across all NearNbr structures in the constructed tree is $O(M n \log n)$, where $M = O(\log(n)/\gamma)$ is the per-point replication factor.
nodes.statement_clean: Bounds the total replication of points across all NearNbr structures in the construction tree.

nodes.name: Construction complexity of nearest-neighbor data structure
nodes.statement: If $S(n,c,f)$ and $T(n,c,f)$ are convex, the data structure of Algorithm 2 uses $O(S(n,c,f)/\gamma \cdot \log^2 n)$ space and is constructed in expected time $O(T(n,c,f)/(\gamma \log^2 n) + n \log n (Q(n,c,f) + D(n,c,f)))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Construction time and space bounds for the recursive nearest-neighbor data structure.

nodes.name: Search performs $O(\log n)$ NearNbr queries
nodes.statement: The S EARCH procedure performs at most $O(\log n)$ NearNbr queries and distance computations.
nodes.statement_clean: Bounds the number of NearNbr queries during a single approximate-NN search.

nodes.name: Approximation guarantee of Search
nodes.statement: S EARCH reports a $(1+\gamma)^2 c$-approximate nearest neighbor of $q$ in $P$ with failure probability at most $O(1/E)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Search returns a (1+gamma)^2 c-approximate nearest neighbor with bounded failure probability.

nodes.name: Reduction from approximate nearest to near neighbor (no preprocessing)
nodes.statement: Given a $(c,r)$-NN data structure with space $S(n,c,f)$, query $Q(n,c,f)$, failure $f$, there is a $c(1+O(\gamma))$-NN data structure with query $O(\log n) Q(n,c,f)$, failure $O(f \log n)$, space $O(S(n,c,f)/\gamma \cdot \log^2 n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Black-box reduction from approximate-near to approximate-nearest neighbor, transferring time/space bounds.
assumptions: $(c,r)$-near neighbor data structure with $S(n,c,f), Q(n,c,f), f$
conclusions: $c(1+O(\gamma))$-NN data structure with query time $O(\log n) Q(n,c,f)$

nodes.name: Reduction from approximate nearest to near neighbor (with preprocessing)
nodes.statement: Under adaptive $(c,r)$-NN with construction $T$, space $S$, query $Q$, deletion $D$, one can build in expected time $O(T/(\gamma \log^2 n) + (Q+D) n \log n)$ a $c(1+O(\gamma))$-NN structure with query $O(\log n) Q$, failure $O(f \log n)$, space $O(S/\gamma \cdot \log^2 n)$, and number of stored points $O((n/\gamma) \log^2 n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Variant of the reduction giving construction-time guarantees, requiring an adaptive near-neighbor base.
assumptions: $(c,r)$-near neighbor data structure with $T,S,Q,D,f$ that is adaptive wrt sets of size $n^{O(1)}$

nodes.name: Coordinate range reduction (Bern)
nodes.statement: Fix $a > 1$. If there is a $(c,1)$-NN structure on $[0,a]^d$ under $\ell_1$ with bounds $S, Q, f$, then there is one for $\ell_1^d$ with the same asymptotic bounds and failure $f + 1/a$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reduces (c,1)-NN over R^d to (c,1)-NN over a bounded cube via random grid translation.

nodes.name: Reduction to Hamming cube
nodes.statement: If there is a $(c,r)$-NN structure on a $dM$-dim Hamming cube ($M = O(ad/\delta)$) with bounds $S, Q, f$, then there is a $(c(1+\delta), 1)$-NN for $\ell_1^d$ with the same asymptotic bounds and failure $f + 1/a$.
nodes.statement_clean: Embeds (c,1)-NN over l_1^d into Hamming-cube near neighbor via discretization and unary encoding.

nodes.name: Oblivious LSH guarantee
nodes.statement: For an $(r, cr, p_1, p_2)$-sensitive family $\mathcal{H}$ with $\rho = \log(1/p_1)/\log(1/p_2)$, there is a fully dynamic $(c,r)$-NN structure with query time $O(n^\rho/p_1)$ distance computations and $O(n^{1+\rho}/p_1)$ space; failure probability $\le 1/3 + 1/e$.
nodes.statement_clean: The classical LSH theorem: an (r,cr,p1,p2)-sensitive family yields an (c,r)-NN data structure with query and space exponents controlled by rho.

nodes.name: Dependence on $p_1, p_2$
nodes.statement: The conference paper [35] implicitly assumed $p_1, p_2$ bounded away from $0$. Although true for the LSH families described here, this need not hold in general; this paper makes the dependence explicit.
nodes.statement_clean: Notes that an implicit assumption in earlier work is made explicit here.

nodes.name: Adaptive amplification by independent copies
nodes.statement: There exists an absolute constant $c$ such that for $I = c \log(m+n)$ independent copies, $\Pr[\forall p \in P, q \in Q, \exists t : E_1(q,p) \wedge E_2(q) \text{ holds for } Z_t] \ge 1 - 1/n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Running c log(n+m) independent LSH copies upgrades correctness to hold uniformly over all (p,q) pairs.

nodes.name: Adaptive LSH data structure
nodes.statement: For any $P$ of size $n$, $Q$ of size $m$, the data structure obtained by running $c \log(n+m)$ copies of the algorithm of Theorem 3.4 is adaptive wrt $P,Q$ with failure probability $\le 1/n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Adaptive variant of the LSH data structure obtained by running multiple independent copies.

nodes.name: Coordinate-projection LSH for Hamming
nodes.statement: For Hamming distance over $\Sigma^d$, the family $\mathcal{H} = \{h_i : (b_1,\dots,b_d) \mapsto b_i, i = 1,\dots,d\}$ is $(r, rc, 1 - r/d, 1 - rc/d)$-sensitive.
nodes.statement_clean: Single-coordinate projections form an LSH family for Hamming distance with explicit collision probabilities.

nodes.name: Padding to bound $p_1, p_2$ away from $0$
nodes.statement: Padding inputs with $0$-valued dummy coordinates increases $d$ by a constant factor and ensures $p_1, p_2$ in the family above are bounded away from $0$, so dependence on these can be dropped.
nodes.statement_clean: Notes a padding trick that removes dependence on collision probabilities.

nodes.name: $(c,r)$-NN in Hamming with $n^{1+1/c}$ space
nodes.statement: For any $c > 1$, there is a $(c,r)$-NN algorithm in Hamming metric over $\Sigma^d$ using $O(n^{1+1/c})$ space and $O(n^{1/c})$ distance/hash computations per query/update (each taking $O(d)$ resp. $O(d/r \cdot \log n)$ time).
nodes.statement_clean: LSH+Hamming yields a (c,r)-NN data structure with exponent 1/c in n.

nodes.name: Logarithmic ratio bound
nodes.statement: For $x \in [0,1)$ and $t \ge 1$ with $1 - tx > 0$: $\log(1-x)/\log(1-tx) \le 1/t$.
nodes.statement_clean: Calculus claim used to bound the LSH exponent rho by 1/c.

nodes.name: $(c(1+\delta),1)$-NN in $\ell_1^d$ via LSH
nodes.statement: For $c > 1, \delta > 0$, there is a randomized data structure for $(c(1+\delta), 1)$-NN over $\le n$ points in $\ell_1^d$ using $O(dn + n^{1+1/c})$ space with $O((d/\delta) n^{1/c} \log n)$ query/update time.
nodes.statement_clean: Composing the Hamming reduction with the Hamming LSH gives an l_1 near-neighbor data structure.

nodes.name: $c(1+\gamma)(1+\delta)$-NN in $\ell_1^d$
nodes.statement: For $c > 1, \delta > 0, \gamma \in (1/n, 1)$, there is a randomized $c(1+\gamma)(1+\delta)$-NN data structure over $n$ points in $\ell_1^d$ using $O(dn + n^{1+1/c} \log^2 n \log\log n / \gamma)$ space and $O((d/\delta) n^{1/c} \log^2 n \log\log n)$ query time.
nodes.statement_clean: Combines LSH near-neighbor (Theorem 3.12) with the reduction of Theorem 2.9 to get an l_1 nearest-neighbor data structure.

nodes.name: Adaptive $(c(1+\delta),1)$-NN in $\ell_1^d$
nodes.statement: There is a randomized $(c(1+\delta),1)$-NN over $n$ points in $\ell_1^d$ using $O(dn + n^{1+1/c} \log n)$ space and $O((d/\delta) n^{1/c} \log^2 n)$ query/update time, adaptive wrt $|Q| = n^{O(1)}$ with failure $\le 1/n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Adaptive variant of the LSH near-neighbor data structure for l_1.

nodes.name: Bucketing for $(c,r)$-NN in $\ell_s^d$
nodes.statement: For $0 < \varepsilon < 1/2$, there is a $(c,r)$-NN algorithm in $\ell_s^d$ using $O(n) \times O(1/\varepsilon)^d$ space and preprocessing time, and $O(d)$ query time.
nodes.statement_clean: Grid-bucketing yields fast O(d) queries for (c,r)-NN at the cost of (1/eps)^d space.

nodes.name: $(c,r)$-NN in $\ell_s^d$ via JL dimensionality reduction
nodes.statement: For $s \in \{1,2\}$ and $0 < \varepsilon < 1/2$, there is an algorithm for $(c,r)$-NN in $\ell_s^d$ using $n^{O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/\varepsilon^2)}$ space and preprocessing, with query time $O(d \log n / \varepsilon^2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combining JL dimension reduction with bucketing removes the curse of dimensionality at the cost of a log(1/eps)/eps^2 exponent.

nodes.name: Approximate Voronoi diagram
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C > 0$ such that for $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\varepsilon \in (0, 1/2)$, one can compute an approximate Voronoi diagram of $P$ of size $O(n (C/\varepsilon)^{d+1} \log^2 n)$ in time $O(n (C/\varepsilon)^{d+1} \log^3 n)$, where every cell is a cube or set difference of two cubes and is labeled with a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate nearest neighbor.
nodes.statement_clean: Constructs an approximate Voronoi diagram in which each cell is labeled with a (1+eps)-approximate nearest neighbor.

nodes.name: Volume of $\ell_s$-ball
nodes.statement: $V_s^d(R) = (2 \Gamma(1+1/s))^d / \Gamma(1+n/s) \cdot R^d$; in particular $V_2^d(R) = (2 \pi^{d/2})/(d \, \Gamma(d/2)) \cdot R^d$.
nodes.statement_clean: Closed-form volume of an l_s ball in d dimensions.
nodes.origin_citation: Pisier, The Volume of Convex Bodies (cited as [55])

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss embedding $\ell_s \to \ell_1$
nodes.statement: For any $d, \gamma$, there exists a mapping $f : \ell_s^d \to \ell_1^{d'}$ with $d' = O(d \log(1/\gamma)/\gamma^2)$ such that $\|p-q\|_s \le \|f(p)-f(q)\|_1 \le (1+\gamma) \|p-q\|_s$ for all $p,q$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cited low-distortion embedding from l_s into l_1 used to extend l_1 results to l_s for s in [1,2].

nodes.name: Approximate-MST guarantee
nodes.statement: Algorithm 4 (Kruskal-style with A PPROXIMATE CC at increasing radii) reports a $c(1 + 2\gamma)$-approximate MST.
nodes.statement_clean: The Kruskal-style algorithm using approximate CC subroutines returns an MST within factor c(1+2gamma).

nodes.name: Approximate MST in $\ell_1^d$
nodes.statement: A $c(1+2\gamma)$-approximate MST of $n$ points in $\ell_1^d$ can be computed in $O(d n^{1+1/c} \log^3(n)/\gamma)$ time.
nodes.statement_clean: MST approximation result obtained by plugging the LSH-based near-neighbor structure into the Kruskal-style algorithm.

nodes.name: A PPROXIMATE CC
nodes.statement: Computes a partition $\mathcal{P}$ with $CC_P(r) \sqsubseteq \mathcal{P} \sqsubseteq CC_P(cr)$ via repeated NearNbr queries with deletions, simulating a graph-search.
output: Partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $P$ refining $CC_P(cr)$ and refined by $CC_P(r)$
nodes.pseudocode: Construct NearNbr$(P,c,r,f)$. While $P \ne \emptyset$: pick $p \in P$, delete $p$, set $S = \{p\}, C = \emptyset$; repeat: pick $q \in S$, add $q$ to $C$, delete $q$ from $S$, repeat: $p' \gets$ NearNbr$(q)$; if $p'$ not null: add $\{q,p'\}$ to $E'$, delete $p'$ from $P$ and NearNbr, add $p'$ to $S$ until $p'$ null; until $S = \emptyset$; add $C$ to $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: C ONSTRUCT (recursive nearest-neighbor data structure)
nodes.statement: Recursively partitions $P$ via approximate-CC at radii $r^*_{\mathrm{bot}}, r^*_{\mathrm{med}}$ and builds an INearNbr over $[r^*_{\mathrm{bot}}/2, r^*_{\mathrm{top}}]$ at each tree node.
output: Search tree of NearNbr / INearNbr data structures answering $(1+O(\gamma))c$-NN queries
nodes.pseudocode: If $|P|=1$: store $P$ and return. Repeat: compute $r^*_{\mathrm{med}}, r^*_{\mathrm{bot}}, r^*_{\mathrm{top}}$ (Lemma 2.1, Claim 2.2); compute partitionings $\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P}'$ via A PPROXIMATE CC at $r^*_{\mathrm{bot}}$ and $r^*_{\mathrm{med}}$; until $|\mathcal{P}'| \le n/2$ and $|P_i| \le n/2$. For each $i$: select representative $p'_i$, build INearNbr over $P_i$ with range $[r^*_{\mathrm{bot}}/2, r^*_{\mathrm{top}}]$, recurse on $P_1,\dots,P_k$ and $P' = \{p'_1,\dots,p'_{k'}\}$.

nodes.name: S EARCH (approximate nearest neighbor)
nodes.statement: Recursively traverses the C ONSTRUCT tree using the three INearNbr outcomes to either descend into a child set $P_i$, descend into the representatives $P'$, or directly report a $(1+\gamma)c$-approximate NN.
output: A $(1+\gamma)^2 c$-approximate nearest neighbor of $q$ in $P$
nodes.pseudocode: If $|P|=1$: report the point. Else: INearNbr$(q)$ (Lemma 2.4); if outcome (i): let $P_i$ be the set with $D_{P_i}(q) \le r^*_{\mathrm{bot}}/2$; recurse Search$(P_i, q)$. Elif outcome (ii): recurse Search$(P', q)$. Elif outcome (iii): report the $p'$ found by INearNbr.

nodes.name: LSH near neighbor data structure
nodes.statement: Concatenate $k$ hash functions from $\mathcal{H}$ to form $g_j$; sample $L$ such $g_j$; bucket each $p \in P$ under $g_1(p), \dots, g_L(p)$; on query, scan $g_1(q), \dots, g_L(q)$, stopping after $3L$ candidates.
output: Either a point $p_j$ with $D(p_j, q) \le r_2$, or null
nodes.pseudocode: Preprocessing: choose $L$ functions $g_j(p) = (h_{i_1}(p), \dots, h_{i_k}(p))$ with $h_{i_t} \in \mathcal{H}$ uniformly at random; store pointer to each $p \in P$ in buckets $g_1(p), \dots, g_L(p)$; keep only non-empty buckets via standard hashing. Query$(q)$: scan candidates from $g_1(q), \dots, g_L(q)$ until at least $3L$ candidates seen; for each candidate $p_j$ check $D(p_j, q) \le r_2$ and return on success; else return null.

nodes.name: Approximate minimum spanning tree (Kruskal-style)
nodes.statement: Kruskal-style algorithm that, at each scale $r_i = r/(1+\gamma)^{M-i}$, calls A PPROXIMATE CC and merges newly connected components.
output: Set of edges $E$ forming a $c(1+2\gamma)$-approximate MST
nodes.pseudocode: $E \gets \emptyset$. Pick $q \in P$, let $r$ be max $D(q,p)$ over $p \in P$. Define $r_i = r/(1+\gamma)^{M-i}$ for $i = 0,\dots,M$, $M = \log_{1+\gamma}(n/\gamma)$. Let $\mathcal{P} = \{\{p_1\}, \dots, \{p_n\}\}$. For $i = 0, \dots, M$: invoke A PPROXIMATE CC$(P, c, r_i)$ producing edges $E'$; for each $e = \{u,v\} \in E'$: if $u, v$ are in different sets of $\mathcal{P}$: merge their sets, add $e$ to $E$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Pick $p$ uniformly at random and define $r^*_{\mathrm{med}}$ as the median of $D(p,p')$ over $p' \in P$; $p$ falls in the largest CC with probability $> 1/2$, giving the two-sided bound on $r^*_{\mathrm{med}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: Build $M$ NearNbr structures at radii $r_i = a(1+\gamma)^{i-1}/c$; binary search reveals the smallest $i$ with $Z_{i+1}$ returning a point, yielding the claimed approximation guarantee.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.5
nodes.statement: Solves the recurrence $B(n) = \max [\sum_i B(n_i) + B(k') + n]$ subject to $k' \le n/2$, $\sum n_i = n$; convexity of negated entropy gives $B(n) \le C n \log n + 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.8
nodes.statement: Case analysis on the INearNbr outcome combined with induction on tree depth; choosing $\lambda = O(\log n / \gamma)$ keeps the cumulative blow-up at $(1+\gamma)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.4
nodes.statement: Set $k = \lceil \log_{1/p_2} n \rceil$ to bound expected far-collisions, and $L = n^\rho/p_1$ to bound the chance no near collision occurs; events $E_1, E_2$ each succeed with probability $> 1/2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.10
nodes.statement: Estimate $\rho = \ln(1/p_1)/\ln(1/p_2) \le (1-p_1)/(1-p_2) = 1/c$ using Claim 3.11; the running time and space follow from Theorem 3.4.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Compare $e_t$ produced by the algorithm against the exact-Kruskal $e^*_t$; total cost from stage $0$ is $\le c\gamma$ MST cost, and $\mathrm{cost}(e_t) \le c(1+\gamma) \mathrm{cost}(e^*_t)$ for $t > 0$.

nodes.name: Pick random pivot $p$
nodes.statement: Select $p \in P$ uniformly at random; with probability $> 1/2$, $p$ lies in the largest connected component $C$ of $UB_P(r_{\mathrm{med}})$.

nodes.name: Lower bound: $r_{\mathrm{med}} \le r^*_{\mathrm{med}}$
nodes.statement: $p$ together with the $n/2$ closest points to $p$ induces a CC in $UB_P(r^*_{\mathrm{med}})$ of size $n/2 + 1$, so by minimality of $r_{\mathrm{med}}$, $r_{\mathrm{med}} \le r^*_{\mathrm{med}}$.

nodes.name: Upper bound: $r^*_{\mathrm{med}} \le (n-1) r_{\mathrm{med}}$
nodes.statement: All points in $C$ lie within $(n-1) r_{\mathrm{med}}$ of $p$ (by traversing the connected component); since $|C| > n/2$, the median distance is $\le (n-1) r_{\mathrm{med}}$.

nodes.name: Bound far collisions
nodes.statement: With $k = \lceil \log_{1/p_2} n \rceil$, $\Pr[g(p') = g(q)] \le p_2^k = 1/n$ for any far point $p'$; expected number of far collisions across $L$ functions is $\le L$.

nodes.name: Apply Markov to $E_2$
nodes.statement: By Markov's inequality, the probability of $> 3L$ far collisions is $< 1/3$, so $\Pr[E_2(q)] \ge 2/3$.

nodes.name: Bound near-collision probability
nodes.statement: $\Pr[g_j(p^*) = g_j(q)] \ge p_1^k \ge p_1 \cdot n^{-\rho}$, so $\Pr[\exists j: g_j(p^*) = g_j(q)] \ge 1 - (1 - p_1 n^{-\rho})^L$.

nodes.name: Choose $L = n^\rho/p_1$ to ensure $E_1$
nodes.statement: Setting $L = n^\rho/p_1$ gives $\Pr[E_1(q,p^*)] \ge 1 - 1/e$.

nodes.name: Construct NearNbr structure
nodes.statement: Construct a NearNbr$(P, c, r, f)$ data structure for $P$.

nodes.name: Outer loop over remaining points
nodes.statement: While $P \ne \emptyset$: select any $p \in P$, delete $p$ from $P$ and the NearNbr structure, initialize $S = \{p\}$, $C = \emptyset$, then run the inner BFS loop.

nodes.name: Inner BFS via NearNbr
nodes.statement: While $S \ne \emptyset$: pick $q \in S$, add to $C$, delete from $S$; repeatedly query NearNbr$(q)$, and while it returns a non-null $p'$, add edge $\{q,p'\}$ to $E'$, delete $p'$ from $P$ and NearNbr, add $p'$ to $S$.

nodes.name: Emit completed component
nodes.statement: When $S$ empties, add $C$ to the partition $\mathcal{P}$ and continue the outer loop.

nodes.name: Sample $L$ hash functions
nodes.statement: Independently sample $L$ functions $g_j(p) = (h_{i_1}(p),\dots,h_{i_k}(p))$ where each $h_{i_t}$ is drawn from $\mathcal{H}$ uniformly at random.

nodes.name: Bucket data points
nodes.statement: For each $p \in P$, store a pointer to $p$ in buckets $g_1(p), \dots, g_L(p)$; retain only non-empty buckets via standard hashing.

nodes.name: Query: scan candidates
nodes.statement: On query $q$, brute-force scan candidates from buckets $g_1(q), \dots, g_L(q)$, interrupting after the first $3L$ candidates encountered.

nodes.name: Return point or null
nodes.statement: If any scanned $p_j$ satisfies $D(p_j, q) \le r_2$ return $p_j$; else return null.

nodes.name: Initialize edge set and scale
nodes.statement: Set $E \gets \emptyset$, pick $q \in P$, $r \gets \max_{p \in P} D(q,p)$, define $r_i = r/(1+\gamma)^{M-i}$ for $i = 0, \dots, M = \log_{1+\gamma}(n/\gamma)$, and start with the singleton partition $\mathcal{P} = \{\{p_1\}, \dots, \{p_n\}\}$.

nodes.name: Iterate over scales
nodes.statement: For $i = 0, \dots, M$: invoke A PPROXIMATE CC$(P, c, r_i)$ to get an edge set $E'$.

nodes.name: Merge components
nodes.statement: For each edge $e = \{u,v\} \in E'$ whose endpoints lie in different sets of $\mathcal{P}$: merge the sets and add $e$ to $E$.

edges.note: Indirectly: AP310.5 uses AP310.1 which uses NearNbr; the LSH AP310.4 instantiates the near-neighbor primitive feeding the MST chain.
